candidate_relations.reason: Bardet-Biedl syndrome shares rod-cone dystrophy, obesity, and intellectual disability but characteristically includes polydactyly, renal anomalies, and hypogonadism. The clinical record features transient neutropenia, microcephaly, joint hyperextensibility, specific facial dysmorphism (bushy eyebrows, beak-shaped nose, ogival palate, short upturned philtrum), and appropriate social behavior — hallmarks of Cohen syndrome, not BBS. BBS is a related but incompatible syndromic diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Bardet-Biedl syndrome is a different ciliopathy syndrome with overlapping features but distinct defining criteria
